### Observed differences

- A02 disappears from the log. In the earlier window it was present in every one of the 200 traces, exactly once per trace, at an early relative position (mean about 0.12 into the case); in the later window it is not observed in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, POS001]
- The relations around A02 collapse accordingly. Before, A02 co-occurred with A01, A03 and A04 in all traces (it ran before A01 in about 90 in 100 cases; with A03 the order was mixed, roughly 50/50; with A04 it preceded in about 47 in 100 cases and was interleaved in the rest) and with A05 in about 47 in 100 traces. In the later window A01, A03 and A04 still occur in every trace but never together with A02, and A05 occurs in about half the traces, again never with A02. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]
- A03's outgoing transitions no longer include A02: before, about 38 in 100 of A03's outgoing transitions went to A02 (besides A05 at 23%, A04 at 18% and A01 at 18%); in the later window the shares go to A05 (35%), A01 (31%) and A04 (28%) instead. A02's own outgoing profile is empty, consistent with the activity not being observed at all. [DIR002, DIR001]
- Downstream work sits earlier in the case: A03's mean relative position falls from about 0.11 to about 0.04, A04's from about 0.60 to about 0.53, and the gap between A03 and A04 shortens, with distances of 1–2 steps now carrying about 35 in 100 observations versus about 23 in 100 before. [POS002, POS003, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A02, previously a mandatory once-per-case activity executed early in every case, is no longer executed in the later window. Participation fell from 200 of 200 traces to 0 of 200, all four observed relations involving A02 changed from full or frequent co-occurrence to A02 being absent while its partners continue unchanged (A01, A03 and A04 in every trace, A05 in about half), and A03's exits that previously led to A02 now lead to A01, A04 and A05. The earlier positions of A03 and A04 and the shorter A03–A04 gap are consistent with the loss of an early activity shifting subsequent work forward. The evidence is direct (occurrence, relation and direction data on A02 itself) and consistent across eleven qualifying items, far above the roughly 0.15 items expected by chance for the 30 units tested. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, DIR001, DIR002, POS002, POS003, LAG001]

Limitation: zero participation strictly shows only that A02 was not observed in the later window; the evidence cannot distinguish a removal from A02 having become conditional and not triggering in this sample, or a change in how A02 events were recorded. Position and gap measures use event positions, not clock time. [OCC001, POS002, LAG001]

message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 30 units tested, 11 items qualified, 0.15 expected by chance. Only control_flow family present. 11 items vs 0.15 expected — that's many times larger (about 73x). So the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. This means we go beyond "insufficient evidence" based on count.

Wait, but the evidence list contains 11 items: POS002, POS001, REL004, POS003, DIR001, REL001, LAG001, DIR002, REL002, OCC001, REL003. Yes, 11 items. Screening says 11 items qualified, 0.15 expected. So the count is many times larger than chance expectation. So we judge by directness, consistency, and ability to rule out competing explanations.

Now let's understand the behaviour.

Key observations:

OCC001: A02 — before: mean occurrences per trace 1.0, trace participation 1.0 (i.e., A02 occurred in 100% of traces, exactly once per trace). After: 0.0 participation, 0.0 mean. So A02 disappeared entirely in the later window. Support before 200, after 0.

POS001: A02 position — before support 1.0 (present in all traces), mean position ~0.12 (early in trace). After support 0.0 — A02 not observed. Consistent with disappearance.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A02 — before: A01 0.18, A03 0.40, A04 0.30, A05 0.12. After: empty profile (A02 not observed, so no outgoing transitions). Consistent with disappearance.

REL001: A01–A02 — before: co-occurrence 1.0, B_before_A (A02 before A01) 0.9, A_before_B 0.1. After: A_only 1.0 — A01 occurs in all traces but A02 never does; they never co-occur. So A01 still always occurs, A02 gone.

REL002: A02–A03 — before: co-occurrence 1.0, A_before_B (A02 before A03) 0.49, B_before_A (A03 before A02) 0.51 — mixed order. After: B_only 1.0 — A03 occurs in all traces, A02 never. So A03 still always occurs.

REL003: A02–A04 — before: co-occurrence 1.0, A_before_B 0.47, interleaved_or_repeated 0.53. After: B_only 1.0 — A04 always occurs, A02 never.

REL004: A02–A05 — before: co-occurrence 0.465, A_only 0.535 (A02 occurs without A05 in ~53.5% of traces), B_only 0, A_before_B 0.385, B_before_A 0.08. After: B_only 0.51, neither 0.49. So in the later window, A05 occurs in about 51% of traces (without A02), and in ~49% of traces neither A02 nor A05 occurs. Interesting: A05 participation dropped from 46.5% (co-occurrence) to 51%? Wait: before, A05 occurred in co-occurrence 0.465 + B_only 0 = 46.5% of traces. After, A05 occurs in B_only 0.51 = 51% of traces. So A05's participation is roughly similar (~46.5% → ~51%). A02 went from 100% to 0%.

So the main story: A02 was a mandatory activity (in every trace, exactly once, early at mean position ~0.12) in the earlier window, and in the later window A02 is not observed at all. Its successors (A01, A03, A04, A05) no longer receive flow from A02; A03's outgoing distribution shifted away from A02 (which was 38% of A03's outgoing transitions before) toward A01, A04, A05.

DIR002: A03's outgoing transitions — before: A02 0.38, A04 0.18, A01 0.175, A05 0.23, A07 0.02, A06 0.015. After: A07 0.035, A04 0.28, A06 0.03, A01 0.305, A05 0.35. So A03→A02 disappeared (A02 gone), and shares redistributed to A01, A04, A05 (and slightly A06, A07).

POS002: A03 position — before mean ~0.109, q75 0.2; after mean ~0.041, q75 0.0. So A03 moved earlier in terms of relative position (mean position decreased). Hmm, position here is normalized position within trace presumably. A03 now occurs earlier in traces.

POS003: A04 position — before mean ~0.60, median 0.625; after mean ~0.525, median ~0.571. Slightly earlier.

LAG001: A03→A04 lag — before: distances 1–5 with mass at 3–4 mostly; after: mass shifted to 1–2. So A04 now follows A03 more immediately (shorter gap).

So the picture: A02 was removed (or became unobserved) from the process. A02 was early (mean relative position ~0.12), always present exactly once, and had outgoing transitions to A01 (18%), A03 (40%), A04 (30%), A05 (12%). After removal, A03 comes earlier (mean position ~0.04), A04 slightly earlier, and A03→A04 gaps shortened. A03's outgoing transitions redistributed from A02 to A01/A04/A05.

Hypothesis: A02 was removed from the process (became optional/skipped entirely, or removed). This is a participation change: an activity that was in 100% of traces is now in 0%. That's direct evidence from OCC001 (participation 1.0 → 0.0), POS001 (support 1.0 → 0.0), DIR001 (empty outgoing profile), REL001/REL002/REL003/REL004 (co-occurrence collapse to A_only or B_only).

This is a "supported hypothesis": the evidence directly and consistently shows A02 disappeared. Multiple independent-ish indicators (occurrence, position support, direction profile empty, four relation pairs) all consistent. The screening count (11 vs 0.15 expected) is many times larger than chance.

But wait — the instruction: "Zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window." The main hypothesis: A02, previously executed once in every case early in the process, is no longer observed in any case in the later window — an activity disappeared (or became entirely skipped). The relations confirm: A01, A03, A04 still occur in every case but never together with A02; A05 occurs in about half the cases without A02.

Also note REL004: before, A02 and A05 co-occurred in 46.5% of traces; A02 occurred without A05 in 53.5%. After, A05 occurs in 51% of traces, neither in 49%. So A05's participation stayed roughly similar (~46.5% → ~51%). This shows the rest of the process continued: A01, A03, A04 still in 100% of traces, A05 in ~half.

Competing explanation: sampling — could A02 be a rare variant that just didn't appear? No — A02 was in 100% of 200 traces before. With 200 traces and prior participation 100%, absence in 200 traces is extremely unlikely by chance. However, we can't distinguish "removed" from "became conditional and never triggered" from a data-capture change. The evidence supports "A02 is no longer executed" as a possibility.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly and consistently shows A02's disappearance: participation 100% → 0%, empty outgoing profile, four relation pairs collapsing from co-occurrence to single-activity patterns. Screening: 11 items vs 0.15 expected — many times larger.

Now, is there anything else? The secondary items POS002, POS003, LAG001, DIR002 describe downstream reconfiguration: A03 earlier, A04 earlier, A03→A04 closer, A03's outputs redistributed away from A02. These are part of the same underlying change (A02 removal) — I can fold them into the main hypothesis as consistent consequences, or report under "Other differences". The instruction: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:'". The position shifts and DIR redistribution are arguably consequences of the same change. I think I can present the main hypothesis as A02's disappearance, and mention the downstream shifts as consistent consequences (part of the same hypothesis — the process reconfigured around the missing A02). Actually, the DIR002 redistribution is directly about A02 (A03→A02 edge vanished), so it's part of the main story. POS002/POS003/LAG001 are downstream timing/position shifts consistent with the removal.

Hmm, but should the main hypothesis include the position shifts? The hypothesis is "A02 was removed / no longer executed". The position shifts are corroborating. I'll state the main hypothesis with A02's disappearance, note the downstream shifts as consistent with it, and put anything not part of it under "Other differences". Actually everything fits the one story. Maybe "Other differences" isn't needed, or I could note that A05's participation remained roughly stable. Let me think if there's anything that doesn't fit.

REL004 after: neither 0.49 — in ~49% of traces neither A02 nor A05 occurs. Before, neither was 0. So A05 was in 46.5% before, 51% after — stable. Fine.

One caution: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires..." — not applicable here; this is an activity disappearing, which is "activities were added or removed, became optional or mandatory". Good.

Also note: DIR shares are over outgoing transitions, not cases. DIR001 after profile is empty because A02 was not observed — I should note that an empty profile doesn't show edges are absent, but combined with OCC001 (A02 not observed at all), it's consistent.
